The data SHOULD NOT include encodings of the Unicode [Unicode] code points listed below. If a receiver (Server or Client) receives a Control Packet containing any of them it MAY close the Network Connection:

U+0001..U+001F control characters 
U+007F..U+009F control characters 
Code points defined in the Unicode specification [Unicode] to be non-characters (for example U+0FFFF)
requirements.condition: When encoding string data in an MQTT Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Avoid encoding Unicode code points U+0001 through U+001F.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The data SHOULD NOT contain encodings of U+0001 through U+001F.
requirements.why_checkable: A generated or captured encoded string can be decoded and checked for any code point in the stated closed range.

requirements.required_behavior: The receiver is permitted, but not required, to close the Network Connection.

requirements.why_checkable: A decoder test can inject the exact byte sequence at arbitrary string positions and inspect the resulting code point.

An MQTT Control Packet consists of up to three parts, always in the following order as illustrated in Figure 2.1 - Structure of an MQTT Control Packet.

Figure 2.1 – Structure of an MQTT Control Packet
Fixed header, present in all MQTT Control Packets
Variable header, present in some MQTT Control Packets
Payload, present in some MQTT Control Packets

requirements.required_behavior: Model the packet using only a fixed header, an optional variable header, and an optional payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not add a fourth structural packet part or a part kind outside the listed three.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet parser or serializer layout can be inspected for the set of structural parts.

requirements.quote: The remaining bits [3-0] of byte 1 in the fixed header contain flags specific to each MQTT Control Packet type as listed in the Table 2.2 - Flag Bits below. requirements.quote: Position: starts at byte 2.
requirements.condition: For the Remaining Length field of an MQTT Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Start the field at byte 2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not start the Remaining Length field at any other byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized byte offset of the field is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is the number of bytes remaining within the current packet, including data in the variable header and the payload. The Remaining Length does not include the bytes used to encode the Remaining Length.
requirements.condition: When calculating Remaining Length
requirements.required_behavior: Set it to the number of bytes after the Remaining Length field, including all variable-header and payload bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared value can be compared with the actual byte count after the field.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is the number of bytes remaining within the current packet, including data in the variable header and the payload. The Remaining Length does not include the bytes used to encode the Remaining Length.
requirements.condition: When calculating Remaining Length
requirements.required_behavior: Exclude every byte used to encode the Remaining Length field itself.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not count Remaining Length encoding bytes in the field value.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field width and the declared remaining byte count can be compared independently.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is the number of bytes remaining within the current packet, including data in the variable header and the payload. The Remaining Length does not include the bytes used to encode the Remaining Length.
requirements.condition: When a packet has neither a variable header nor a payload
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Remaining Length as 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a nonzero Remaining Length when no bytes remain after the field.
requirements.why_checkable: A zero-byte suffix follows directly from defining the value as the count of remaining variable-header and payload bytes.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. Larger values are handled as follows. The least significant seven bits of each byte encode the data, and the most significant bit is used to indicate that there are following bytes in the representation. Thus each byte encodes 128 values and a "continuation bit". The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four.
requirements.condition: When Remaining Length is between 0 and 127 inclusive
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the value in a single byte.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a multi-byte representation for a value up to 127.
requirements.why_checkable: The numeric value and count of encoding bytes can be checked directly.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. Larger values are handled as follows. The least significant seven bits of each byte encode the data, and the most significant bit is used to indicate that there are following bytes in the representation. Thus each byte encodes 128 values and a "continuation bit". The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four.
requirements.condition: When Remaining Length is greater than 127
requirements.required_behavior: Use the multi-byte variable-length representation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a value greater than 127 in a single Remaining Length byte.
requirements.why_checkable: A single byte has only seven data bits because its high bit is the continuation indicator.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. Larger values are handled as follows. The least significant seven bits of each byte encode the data, and the most significant bit is used to indicate that there are following bytes in the representation. Thus each byte encodes 128 values and a "continuation bit". The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four.
requirements.condition: For every byte of the Remaining Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Use the least significant seven bits to encode value data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use bit 7 as a value-data bit.
requirements.why_checkable: Each byte can be masked into its low seven data bits and high continuation bit.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. Larger values are handled as follows. The least significant seven bits of each byte encode the data, and the most significant bit is used to indicate that there are following bytes in the representation. Thus each byte encodes 128 values and a "continuation bit". The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four.
requirements.condition: For a Remaining Length byte when another Remaining Length byte follows
requirements.required_behavior: Set the most significant bit to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set the continuation bit to 0 when another field byte follows.
requirements.why_checkable: The presence of a following field byte can be compared with bit 7 of the current byte.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. Larger values are handled as follows. The least significant seven bits of each byte encode the data, and the most significant bit is used to indicate that there are following bytes in the representation. Thus each byte encodes 128 values and a "continuation bit". The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four.
requirements.condition: For the final byte of the Remaining Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Set the most significant continuation bit to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave the continuation bit set when no further field byte follows.
requirements.why_checkable: Because the high bit indicates that bytes follow, the final byte must clear it; this is testable from the encoded byte sequence.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. Larger values are handled as follows. The least significant seven bits of each byte encode the data, and the most significant bit is used to indicate that there are following bytes in the representation. Thus each byte encodes 128 values and a "continuation bit". The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four.
requirements.condition: For any Remaining Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Use no more than four bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A five-byte or longer Remaining Length field is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoder or serializer can count field bytes before the terminating continuation bit.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. Larger values are handled as follows. The least significant seven bits of each byte encode the data, and the most significant bit is used to indicate that there are following bytes in the representation. Thus each byte encodes 128 values and a "continuation bit". The maximum number of bytes in the Remaining Length field is four.
requirements.condition: For any Remaining Length value
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the value at or below 268435455.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a value greater than 268435455.
requirements.why_checkable: Four bytes with seven data bits each provide 28 value bits, whose maximum unsigned value is 2^28-1.
